1273.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
1273.text: Assertion : In an elastic collision of two billiard balls, the total kinetic energy is conserved during the short time of oscillation of the balls (i.e. when they are in contact). Reason : Energy spent against friction does not follow the law of conservation of energy.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1273.sol: The billiard balls in an elastic collision are in a deformed state. And their total energy is in the form of P.E. and K.E. Thus K.E. is less than the total energy. The energy spent against friction is dissipated in the form of heat which is not available for doing work.

1307.subject: Physics
1307.text: Assertion : A current flows in a conductor only when there is an electric field within the conductor. Reason : The drift velocity of electron in presence of electric field decreases.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1307.sol: In the absence of external electric field, the free electrons move randomly in the conductor, so their drift velocity is zero and therefore there is no current in the conductor. In the presence of electric field, each electron in the conductor experiences a force in a direction opposite to the electric field. Now the free electrons are drifted from negative end to the positive end of the conductor and hence a current starts to flow in the conductor.

79876.sol: In anaphase-I of meiosis homologous chromosomes separate and pass towards different poles of the spindle creating two haploid sets of chromosomes. During anaphase-II of meiosis centromere of two chromatids of a chromosome separate. The separated chromatids become independent daughter chromosome.

80314.subject: Botany
80314.text: In which one of the following, the ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain exposed ?
80314.sol: Gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization. Pinus is a gymnosperm, so its ovules are naked and remain exposed. Funaria is a bryophyte and Selaginella is a pteridophyte, both of which do not produce ovules or seeds. Wolffia is an angiosperm, in which the ovules are enclosed within an ovary wall. Answer: Pinus

120595.subject: Chemistry
120595.text: Which carbohydrate is used by plants to build their cell walls?
120595.sol: Cellulose is used by plants to build their cell walls.

120830.subject: Chemistry
120830.text: What is the classification of carbohydrates based on their behavior on hydrolysis?
120830.sol: The classification of carbohydrates based on their behavior on hydrolysis is into three groups: monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides.

120935.subject: Chemistry

options: Hydrolysis of sucrose reverses the direction of polarized light.
Hydrolysis of sucrose produces equal amounts of dextrorotatory and laevorotatory compounds.
Hydrolysis of sucrose forms glucose and fructose, both of which are laevorotatory.
On hydrolysis sucrose (dextrorotatory), gives glucose (dextrorotatory, + 52.5°) and fructose (laevorotatory, –
120935.sol: Correct Option is : (D) On hydrolysis sucrose (dextrorotatory), gives glucose (dextrorotatory, + 52.5°) and fructose (laevorotatory, – 92.4°). Since laevorotation of fructose is more than the dextrorotation of glucose, the mixture is laevorotatory.

121295.subject: Botany
121295.text: How many flagella do most dinoflagellates have?
121295.sol: These organisms are mostly marine and photosynthetic. They appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells. The cell wallhas stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface. Most of them have two flagella; one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates. Very often, red dinoflagellates (Example: Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides). Toxins released by such large numbers may even ki

121479.subject: Botany
121479.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. Reason: The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
121479.sol: In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid. The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight.

121646.subject: Botany
121646.text: Which one of the following is linked to the discovery of bordeaux mixture as a popular fungicide?
121646.sol: Bordeaux mixture was discovered by Millardet in France in 1882. It is prepared by dissolving 40 g of copper sulphate and 40 g of calcium hydroxide in 5 L of water. It was first used to control downy mildew disease of grape-vine that is caused by a fungus Plasmopara viticola. Black rust of wheat is caused by Puccinia graminis tritici. The use of fungicide dithane Z-78 and dithane M-45 control the disease even at lower concentration. Loose smut of wheat is caused by Ustilago tritici. The use of fungicides (systemic f

121803.subject: Botany
121803.text: How are mosses attached to the soil?
121803.sol: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema stage, which develops directly from a spore. It is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage. The second stage is the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. They consist of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves. They are attached to the soil through multicellular and branched rhizoids. This stage bears the sex orga

122059.subject: Botany
122059.text: Which one of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
122059.sol: Salvinia is a heterosporoues water fern. The microsporangia and megasporangia are borne within special reproductive structure called sporocarps. These are borne terminally in clusters on the segment of submerged leaves. Sporocarps are strictly monosporangiate, i.e., they bear either only microsporangia or megasporangia. Viroids are single stranded RNA molecules. The female reproductive organ is archegonia in gymnosperms.

123514.subject: Botany
123514.text: Species can be identified on the basis of
123514.sol: The prevention of inbreeding between the populations of two different species is known as reproductive isolation. Reproductive isolation leads to the origin of new species.

123886.subject: Botany
123886.text: In oocytes of some vertebrates, a specific stage of prophase I of meiosis can last for months or years. Identify this arrested stage along with its defining chromosomal feature.
options: Diplotene - Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex
Zygotene - Formation of the synaptonemal complex
123886.sol: In oocytes of some vertebrates, the diplotene stage can last for months or years. This arrested stage is known as the dictyotene stage. The beginning of the diplotene stage is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. Terminalisation of chiasmata is the defining feature of diakinesis, not diplotene. Therefore, the correct pairing is Diplotene with the dissolution

123925.subject: Botany
123925.text: Assertion : The number of cells in a multicellular organism is inversely proportional to the size of body. Reason : All the cells in the biological world are of same size.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
123925.sol: The number of cells in a multicellular organism are directly proportional to the size of the body. On the other hand, it is a fact that cells vary greatly in their size.

124054.subject: Botany
124054.text: What is the structure that the cilium and flagellum emerge from?
124054.sol: The central tubules are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a radial spoke. Thus, there are nine radial spokes. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by linkers. Both the cilium and flagellum emerge from centriole-like structure called the basal bodies.

movement of water from cell A to B

The first process takes place in the matrix of the mit

There can be a net gain of 38 ATP molecules during aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose.,In animal cells also, like muscles during exercise, when oxygen is inadequate for cellular respiration pyruvic acid is reduced to lactic acid by lactate dehydrogenase. The reducing agent is NADH+H+ which is reoxidised to NAD+ in both the processes.

125326.subject: Botany
125326.text: What does the process of photosynthesis involve according to Cornelius van Niel?
125326.sol: A milestone contribution to the understanding of photosynthesis was that made by a microbiologist, Cornelius van Niel (1897-1985), who, based on his studies of purple and green bacteria, demonstrated that photosynthesis is essentially a light-dependent reaction in which hydrogen from a suitable oxidisable compound reduces carbon dioxide to carbohydrates. In green plants H2O is the hydrogen donor and is oxidised to O2 . Some organisms do not release O2 during photosynthesis. When H2 S, instead is the hydrogen donor

125545.subject: Botany
125545.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Calvin cycle is described under four stages Reason: Calvin and his co-workers then worked out the whole pathway and showed that the pathway operated in a non cyclic manner
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125545.sol: Calvin cycle can be described under three stages: carboxylation, reduction and regeneration.

Assertion: In Citrus and Mango varieties each ovule contains many embryos, occurance of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony Reason: In species such as Citrus and Mango varieties of the nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac and develop into the embryos

126442.subject: Botany
126442.text: What is the common feature of all compounds found in the acid soluble pool?
options: They have molecular weights ranging from 18 to around 800 daltons
126442.sol: There is one feature common to all those compounds found in the acid soluble pool. They have molecular weights ranging from 18 to around 800 daltons (Da) approximately .The acid insoluble fraction, has only four types of organic compounds i.e., proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids. These classes of compounds with the exception of lipids, have molecular weights in the range of ten thousand daltons and above. For this very reason, biomolecules, i.e., chemical compounds found in living organisms are of

126980.subject: Botany
126980.text: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?
126980.sol: O 3 is a secondary pollutant. It is called a "secondary" pollutant because it is produced when two primary pollutants react in sunlight and stagnant air. These two primary pollutants are nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs)

127155.subject: Botany
127155.text: What is the most well:known pattern in diversity of animals and plants?
127155.sol: The diversity of plants and animals is not uniform throughout the world but shows a rather uneven distribution. For many group of animals or plants, there are interesting patterns in diversity, the most well- known being the latitudinal gradient in diversity. In general, species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles. With very few exceptions, tropics (latitudinal range of 23.5° N to 23.5° S) harbour more species than temperate or polar areas. Colombia located near the equator has ne

127271.subject: Botany
127271.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats. Reason: Rauwolfia vomitoria grows in Western ghats.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127271.sol: The genetic variation shown by the medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges might be in terms of the potency and concentration of the active chemical (reserpine) that the plant produces. The diversity at the species level, for example, the Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats.

Extinction of species due to the loss of another species with which it is closely associa
127337.sol: A - 2: Habitat loss and fragmentation refer to the destruction or division of natural habitats, which reduces species populations and leads to extinction. B - 3: Over-exploitation involves excessive harvesting of species, such as overfishing or hunting, leading to extinction. C - 1: Alien species invasions occur when non-native species are introduced into an ecosystem, where they disrupt local ecosystems and cause the extinction of native species. D - 4: Co-extinctions happen when a species becomes extinct, leading

128184.subject: Zoology
128184.text: Read the following statements regarding connective tissues and choose the incorrect statement.
options: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue that often serves as a support framework for epithelium.
Blood is a specialized connective tissue in which the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins.
The intercellular material of cartilage is solid, pliable and resists compression.
Bones have a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres.
128184.sol: According to NCERT, in all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin. Blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets, but its cells do not secrete structural fibres. Thus, the statement about blood cells secreting structural protein fibres is incorrect. Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue present beneath the skin and serves as a support framework for epithelium. The intercellular materia

128634.subject: Zoology
128634.text: Select the correct statement about hormones and their actions
options: Parathyroid hormone increases K ⁺ absorption of the body.
Insulin and glucagon helps to maintain blood sugar levels.
Old aged people have weak immunity due to increased activity of thymus.
Osteoporosis in women occurs due to increased levels of oestrogens.
128634.sol: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) stimulates the reabsorption of Ca ²⁺ by renal tubules and increases Ca ²⁺ absorption from digested food. It means PTH increases the blood Ca ²⁺ level. Old aged persons have weak immunity because thymus is degenerated in old individuals resulting in a decreased production of thymosin. Oestoporosis in women occurs due to decreased level of estrogen.

128750.subject: Zoology
128750.text: Maximum absorption of water occurs in :
128750.sol: The chief functions of the large intestine are the absorption of water and the elimination of solid wastes. Large intestine is divided into three parts i.e., caecum, colon and rectum. In mammals, colon has essential water absorbing role in preparation of faeces.

129443.subject: Zoology
129443.text: Which part of retina consists of only cones?
129443.sol: Lateral to the blind spot, there is a dipressed area of the retina, called fovea centralis, which contains only cones. Ability for vision is highest in the fovea.

129535.subject: Zoology
129535.text: What is the main function of the Collecting Duct in urine formation?
options: Maintenance of pH and ionic balance
129535.sol: Collecting Duct: This long duct extends from the cortex of the kidnney to the inner parts of the medulla. Large amounts of water could be reabsorbed from this region to produce a concentrated urine. This segment allows passage of small amounts of urea into the medullary interstitium to keep up the osmolarity. It also plays a role in the maintenance of pH and ionic balance of blood by the selective secretion of H+ and K+ ions. Collecting Duct: This long duct extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts o

129932.subject: Zoology
129932.text: What are the values of a, b, c, d and e in mm Hg?
129932.sol: a, b, c, d and e in mm Hg are 0.3, 104, 45, 95, 45 respectively

130409.subject: Zoology
130409.text: Part of Lower Limb Bone A. Thigh 1. Tibia and Fibula B. Knee 2. Patella C. Leg 3 .Femur D. Foot 4. Tarsals, Metatarsals, and Phalanges
130409.sol: Thigh: Contains the femur, the longest bone in the body. Knee: Contains the patella, or kneecap, which protects the knee joint. Leg: Contains the tibia and fibula, forming the lower part of the limb. Foot: Composed of tarsals, metatarsals, and phalanges, forming the structure of the foot.

131148.subject: Zoology
131148.text: Process Description A. Gestation period 1. Vigorous uterine contractions leading to childbirth B. Parturition 2. Average duration of human pregnancy (about 9 months) C. Foetal ejection reflex 3. Initial mild uterine contractions triggered by fully developed foetus and placenta D. Lactation 4. Production of milk towards the end of pregnancy
131148.sol: Gestation period: The period of about 9 months during which the human pregnancy lasts. Parturition: The process of childbirth involving vigorous contractions of the uterus. Foetal ejection reflex: Mild uterine contractions initiated by signals from the foetus and placenta. Lactation: The process of milk production by the mammary glands towards the end of pregnancy

131292.subject: Zoology
131292.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): During spermatogenesis, 50 secondary spermatocytes will produce 100 spermatids. Reason (R): Each secondary spermatocyte undergoes a reductional division to produce two haploid spermatids. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
131292.sol: Assertion (A) is true: Each secondary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis II to produce two spermatids. Therefore, 50 secondary spermatocytes will produce 50 2 = 100 spermatids. Reason (R) is false: Secondary spermatocytes are haploid cells that undergo the second meiotic division (meiosis II) to produce spermatids. Meiosis II is an equational division, not a reductional division. The reductional division (meiosis I) occurs when primary spermatocytes divide to form secondary spermatocytes. Answer: (A) is true but (R) is

131402.subject: Zoology
131402.text: Which nitrogenous base is common for both DNA and RNA?
131402.sol: A nucleotide has three components – a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group. There are two types of nitrogenous bases – Purines (Adenine and Guanine), and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine). Cytosine is common for both DNA and RNA and Thymine is present in DNA. Uracil is present in RNA at the place of Thymine. A nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of 1' C pentose sugar through a N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside, such as adenosine

132044.subject: Zoology
132044.text: What was applied to problems in biology for the first time during Mendel’s investigations?
132044.sol: It was during the mid-nineteenth century that headway was made in the understanding of inheritance. Gregor Mendel, conducted hybridisation experiments on garden peas for seven years (1856-1863) and proposed the laws of inheritance in living organisms. During Mendel’s investigations into inheritance patterns it was for the first time that statistical analysis and mathematical logic were applied to problems in biology . His experiments had a large sampling size, which gave greater credibility to the data that he coll

132107.subject: Zoology
132107.text: What are Mendel's rules of inheritance called today?
132107.sol: Based on his observations on monohybrid crosses Mendel proposed two general rules to consolidate his understanding of inheritance in monohybrid crosses. Today these rules are called the Principles or Laws of Inheritance: the First Law or Law of Dominance and the Second Law or Law of Segregation.

132167.subject: Zoology
132167.text: In the dihybrid cross, what was the observed phenotypic ratio of round, yellow; wrinkled, yellow; round, green; and wrinkled, green?
132167.sol: In the dihybrid cross (Figure 4.7), the phenotypes round, yellow; wrinkled, yellow; round, green and wrinkled, green appeared in the ratio 9:3:3:1 . Such a ratio was observed for several pairs of characters that Mendel studied. The ratio of 9:3:3:1 can be derived as a combination series of 3 yellow: 1 green, with 3 round : 1 wrinkled. This derivation can be written as follows: (3 Round : 1 Wrinkled) (3 Yellow : 1 Green) = 9 Round, Yellow : 3 Wrinkled, Yellow: 3 Round, Green : 1 Wrinkled, Green Based upon such obser

options: Results of a monohybrid cross where the two parents differed in one pairs of contrasting traits: seed colour.
Results of a dihybrid cross where the two parents differed in two pairs of contrasting traits: flower colour a
Results of a dihybrid cross where the two parents differed in two pairs of contrasting traits: seed colour and
Results of a monohybrid cross where the two parents differed in one pairs of contrasting traits: seed shape.

132522.subject: Zoology
132522.text: Read the following statements regarding linkage and recombination and choose the incorrect statement.
options: Alfred Sturtevant used the frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure o
When two genes in a dihybrid cross are situated on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combin
Loosely linked genes grouped on the same chromosome show a higher frequency of recombination compared to tight
Genes that are tightly linked on the same chromosome show a high frequency of non-parental gene combinations.
132522.sol: According to Morgan's experiments on Drosophila, genes that are tightly linked on the same chromosome show very low recombination (non-parental gene combinations) and a very high proportion of parental gene combinations. Therefore, the statement claiming that tightly linked genes show a high frequency of non-parental combinations is incorrect. Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequencies to map gene positions, which is a correct statement. When genes are on the same chromosome, they tend to be inherited togethe

133461.subject: Zoology
133461.text: Type of immunoglobulin Characteristic A. IgG 1. First antibody produced during primary immune response B. IgA 2. Found in mucosal areas like the gut, respiratory tract, and urogenital tract C. IgM 3. Provides long-term immunity; crosses the placenta D. IgE 4. Involved in allergic reactions; binds to mast cells and basophils
133461.sol: IgG is the most abundant immunoglobulin in the blood and is critical for long-term immunity. It is the only immunoglobulin that can cross the placenta, providing passive immunity to the fetus. IgA is primarily found in mucosal areas, such as the gut, respiratory tract, and urogenital tract, and in secretions like saliva, tears, and breast milk. It plays a crucial role in mucosal immunity. IgM is the first antibody produced in response to an infection during the primary immune response. It is also the largest antibo

133528.subject: Zoology
133528.text: Innate immunity consists of different types of barriers that prevent the entry of foreign agents into our body. Which of the following is an incorrectly matched pair of an innate immunity barrier and its example?
133528.sol: Saliva in the mouth, tears from the eyes, and acid in the stomach are examples of physiological barriers that prevent microbial growth. Therefore, matching saliva in the mouth with 'Physical barrier' is incorrect. Physical barriers include the skin on our body and the mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts. Polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils) act as cellular barriers by phagocytosing and destroying microbes. Interferons act as cytokine barriers,

134959.subject: Zoology
134959.text: Match the organism with its use in biotechnology. (a) Bacillus thuringiensis (i) Cloning vector (b) Thermus aquaticus (ii) Construction of first rDNA molecule (c) Agrobacterium tumefaciens (iii) DNA polymerase (d) Salmonella typhimurium (iv) Cry proteins
134959.sol: The construction of the first recombinant DNA emerged from the possibility of linking a gene–encoding antibiotic resistance with a native plasmid (autonomously replicating circular extrachromosomal DNA) of Salmonella typhimurium . Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer accomplished this in 1972 by isolating the antibiotic resistance gene by cutting out a piece of DNA from a plasmid that was responsible for conferring antibiotic resistance. The tumor-inducing (Ti) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens has been modifie

135056.subject: Zoology
135056.text: What is the technical term for population size?
135056.sol: The size of the population tells us a lot about its status in the habitat. Whatever ecological processes we wish to investigate in a population, be it the outcome of competition with another species, the impact of a predator or the effect of a pesticide application, we always evaluate them in terms of any change in the population size. The size, in nature, could be as low as <10 (Siberian cranes at Bharatpur wetlands in any year) or go into millions (Chlamydomonas in a pond). Population size, technically called pop

135439.subject: Zoology
135439.text: Assertion : Ectotherms are able to remain active under cold conditions. Reason : Ectotherms are able to maintain a constant internal temperature, even when the temperature outside fluctuates.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
135439.sol: Ectotherms or cold-blooded animals, cannot regulate their body temperature and are unable to maintain a constant internal temperature. Their body temperature tends to match with the environmental temperature in which they live, (e.g., frogs and snakes). These animals are not able to remain active under cold conditions.

6a16f3257cfacf7984f866cb.subject: Physics
6a16f3257cfacf7984f866cb.text: A deuteron and an alpha particle are accelerated from rest through potential differences V₁ and V₂ respectively. If the de-Broglie wavelength associated with both particles is equal, then the ratio V₁ V₂ is:

95763.text: Match the following and choose the correct option: Column-I (Lichens) Column-II (Habitat) A. Graphis I. Grow on stones or rocks B. Dermatocarpon II. Grow on the bark of trees C. Cladonia III. Grow on soil
options: A - II; B - I; C - III
A - II; B - III; C - II
A - III; B - II; C - I
95763.sol: Lichens are divided into different categories based on their habitat: Saxicolous are the type that grow on stones or rocks e.g., Dermatocarpon. Corticolous are the type that grow on the bark of trees e.g., Grpahis, Usnea, Parmelia etc. Terricolous are the type that grow on soil (terrestrial) e.g., Cladonia. Lignicolous are the type that grow on wood e.g., Calicicum

95902.subject: Botany
95902.text: Read the following statements regarding Euglenoids and select the INCORRECT ones. (i) These are mostly freshwater organisms found in stagnant water. (ii) Their body is covered by a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible. (iii) They are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight but become heterotrophs in the absence of sunlight. (iv) They usually possess two flagella, one long and one shor
95902.sol: Euglenoids are unicellular freshwater organisms with two flagella (one long one short) belonging to the kingdom Protista and are found in stagnant water. These organisms instead of a cell wall possess a protein-rich layer called pellicle, which helps to make their body flexible. They can act as autotrophs in presence of sunlight as well as heterotrophs in absence of it.

95986.subject: Botany
95986.text: Select the incorrect statement with respect to centrioles.
options: They are made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin.
The central part is non-proteinaceous and called the hub.
They form the basal body of cilia or flagella.
95986.sol: The central part of centriole is a proteinaceous structure called the hub.which is connected with peripheral triplets by radial spokes.

96063.subject: Botany
96063.text: Which of the following filamentous structures are a structural component of the centriole?
96063.sol: Cytoplasm consists of different proteinaceous filamentous and tubular structure which are called as cyto skeleton, it includes microtubules and microfilaments. Microtubules are structural component of centriole and flagella.

96107.subject: Botany
96107.text: Which of the following statements about the plasma membrane is TRUE?
options: It allows selected molecules to pass into and out of the cell.
It is a rigid and unmoving layer of phospholipids and protein.
It is a solid layer of protein that protects the contents of the cell.
The plasma membrane of a bacterium has none of the same components as the plasma membrane of an animal cell.
96107.sol: Plasma membrane or the cell membrane which is made up of phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins. It is a semipermeable membrane which allows ions and selected molecules to pass in and out of the cell. In bacteria, the cell wall is attached to the plasma membrane and plays the same role as a semipermeable membrane. The plasma membrane protects the cell from the outside environment.

96220.subject: Botany
96220.text: What is not the incorrect sequence of prophase I of meiosis?
96220.sol: Prophase I of meiosis is of longest duration and is further subdivided into five sub phases: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, diakinesis. Leptotene shows bouquet formation. The pairing of homologous chromosome or synapsis occurs in zygotene. Crossing over occurs in pachytene. Chiasmata formation occurs in diplotene, and terminalisation occurs in diakinesis.

96441.subject: Botany
options: First trophic level of a food chain
Second trophic level of a food chain
Third trophic level of a food chain
Fourth trophic level of a food chain
96441.sol: Producers are the first trophic levels, primary consumers or herbivores are at the second trophic level, secondary consumers or primary carnivores are at the third trophic level, whereas the tertiary consumers or secondary carnivores or scavengers are at the fourth trophic level.

96721.subject: Botany
96721.text: The function of which cell organelle is affected the most due to the deficiency of magnesium?
96721.sol: Magnesium ion is very much necessary for the formation and functioning of the ribosome. Two ribosomal subunits bind to form complete ribosome only in presence of magnesium.

96740.subject: Botany
96740.text: How many of the following statements describing the functions of Mn are true? I. Mn is required during non-cyclic photophosphorylation. II. Mn competes with iron and magnesium for uptake. III. Mn promotes calcium translocation in the shoot apex. IV. Mn is an activator of many respiratory enzymes.
96740.sol: Manganese is absorbed in the form of manganous ions. It activates many enzymes involved in photosynthesis, respiration and nitrogen metabolism. It is involved in photolysis of water during non-cyclic photophosphorylation to liberate oxygen during photosynthesis. Manganese competes with iron and magnesium for uptake and with magnesium for binding with enzymes. Manganese inhibits calcium translocation in shoot apex.

96780.subject: Botany
96780.text: _________ is present in cysteine and methionine and is the main constituent of several coenzymes.
96780.sol: Sulphur is a macromolecule and component of cysteine, methionine, vitamins, ferredoxin and several coenzymes.

96819.subject: Botany
96819.text: How many of the following are the members of the family Fabaceae? Gram, belladonna, arhar, moong, potato, Indigofera , pea, tobacco, Sesbania
96819.sol: Fabaceae is a family of dicot plants, mostly legumes. The members of these families have a distinct floral characteristic which shows vexillary aestivation in the petal arrangement. Some important members of this family are pea, Soyabean, Sesbania , lupin, gram, arhar, moong, Indigofera . The other examples like belladonna, potato, and tobacco belong to the family Solanaceae.

97000.subject: Botany
97000.text: Match the column I with column-II Column-I Column-II Stem tendrils Citrus , Bougainvillea Stem thorns Calotropis , guava Opposite phyllotaxy China rose, mustard Alternate phyllotaxy Gourds, grapevines
97000.sol: Stem tendrils (for climbing) and stem thorns (Help in protection )are aerial stem modification. Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch. phyllotaxy is the arrangement of leaves on a plant stem In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sun flower plants. In opposite type, a pair of leaves arise at each node and lie opposite to each other as in Calotropis and guava plants

97241.subject: Botany
97241.text: Match the following: Column I Column II 1 IAA (i) Herring sperm DNA 2 ABA (ii) Bolting 3 Ethylene (iii) Stomatal closure 4 GA (iv) Weed–free lawns 5 Cytokinin (v) Ripening of fruits
97241.sol: Synthetic auxin 2 , 4 D is used as a weedicide and is used to remove dicot weed from monocot field.ABA commonly called as stress hormone causes closure of stomata. Ethylene is only gaseous hormone and it causes ripening of fruits.GA causes rapid intermodal elongation in genetically dwarf plants or rosette plants, the phenomenon is known as bolting. Cytokinin was first isolated by autoclaving herring fish sperm DNA.

309156.text: Ethyl acetoacetate reacts with acetaldehyde ( CH ₃ CHO ) in the presence of a base and heat. The resulting intermediate is then subjected to acidic hydrolysis followed by heating. The major product formed is:
309156.sol: The reaction between ethyl acetoacetate and acetaldehyde in the presence of a base proceeds via a Knoevenagel condensation followed by a Michael addition of a second molecule of ethyl acetoacetate. This forms a bis-adduct: CH₃CHO + 2 CH₃COCH₂COOC₂H₅ Base CH₃CH(CH(COCH₃)COOC₂H₅)₂ Under the basic conditions and heat, this intermediate undergoes an intramolecular aldol condensation. The enolate formed at one of the acetyl methyl groups attacks the carbonyl carbon of the other acetyl group, forming a six-membered ring.

309433.text: Choose the correct statement regarding the acidic character of acetic acid ( CH ₃ COOH ) and peroxyacetic acid ( CH ₃ COOOH ).
options: Peroxyacetic acid is a weaker acid than acetic acid because its conjugate base is less stable than the acetate
Peroxyacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid because it contains an additional electronegative oxygen

309433.sol: The acidic strength of an acid depends on the stability of its conjugate base. When acetic acid ( CH ₃ COOH ) loses a proton, it forms the acetate ion ( CH ₃ COO ⁻ ). The negative charge on the acetate ion is highly stabilized by resonance, as it is delocalized equally over two electronegative oxygen atoms. When peroxyacetic acid ( CH ₃ COOOH ) loses a proton, it forms the peroxyacetate ion ( CH ₃ COOO ⁻ ). In this ion, the negative charge is localized on the terminal oxygen atom. 309444.text: Identify the major product of the following reaction:
309444.sol: The given reactant is a spiro-1,3-dioxolan-4-one derivative, which contains a lactone (cyclic ester) and an acetal functional group. Lithium aluminum hydride (LAH) is a strong reducing agent that reduces esters to primary alcohols. The reduction of the 1,3-dioxolan-4-one ring with LAH proceeds via the cleavage of the ester C-O bond. The carbonyl carbon is reduced to a hydroxymethyl group ( -CH₂OH ). The remaining hemiacetal intermediate collapses (or hydrolyzes during workup), resulting in a hydroxyl group ( -OH )

309452.subject: Chemistry
309452.text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the preparation and preservation of lemon pickle?
options: Lemon oil acts as a preservative.
Salt plays the same role as sugar in jam.
Chillies are used to kill all germs and bacteria.
Citric acid acts as a preservative.
309452.sol: In the preparation of pickles, salt is added as a preservative. It draws out moisture from the food items through osmosis, thereby reducing the water activity and inhibiting the growth of microorganisms. Similarly, in the preparation of jams, sugar is added which also reduces the moisture content and prevents microbial growth. Thus, salt in pickles plays the same role as sugar in jams. Answer: Salt plays the same role as sugar in jam.

303356.text: A constant upward buoyancy force B is exerted by the atmosphere on a balloon. The air resistance acting on the balloon is proportional to its velocity and opposes its motion. 306297.text: A person is travelling on a spaceship that moves at a speed of 5c/13 . Determine the time interval calculated by this person between consecutive birthday celebrations of his friend on the earth.

If a person is selected at random, what is the sum of the probability that the person likes Tea given that they do not like Coffee, and the probability that the person likes Coffee given that they do not like Tea?
6a7a1ff8d9561d640fbf24da.sol: Let T and C be the events that a randomly selected person likes Tea and Coffee, respectively. Given: P(T) = 0.5 P(C) = 0.6 P(T C) = 0.9 Using the inclusion-exclusion principle: P(T C) = P(T) + P(C) - P(T C) 0.9 = 0.5 + 0.6 - P(T C) P(T C) = 1.1 - 0.9 = 0.2 The probability of liking Tea but not Coffee is: P(T C') = P(T) - P(T C) = 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.3 The probability of liking Coffee but not Tea is: P(C T') = P(C) - P(T C) = 0.6 - 0.2 = 0.4 The probabilities of the complementary events are: P(C') = 1 - P(C) = 1 - 0.6 = 0
